results.title: Jin Air's Busan hub plan faces profitability test
results.content: Jin Air’s plan to develop Gimhae International Airport as its second hub after Incheon International Airport faces a profitability test, as the airline prepares to expand international routes and flight frequencies — primarily to Japan — from Busan next year. The integrated Jin Air plans to increase the number of international routes from Gimhae to 33 from the current 28 and raise weekly flights to 339 from 281, according to the low-cost carrier (LCC). The planned expansion in Busan comes in response to growing local industry concerns ahead of the upcoming launch of the converged Jin Air. Air Busan, whose headquarters is currently located in Busan, will be merged into Jin Air from March 17, and the merged entity’s head office will be based in Seoul. results.title: AI cheating puts Korea's decades-old exam system under scrutiny
results.content: Korea’s decades-old testing system, especially the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), is facing growing scrutiny amid fears of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered cheating. However, even as calls for reform grow, proposed changes face practical hurdles and offer no guarantee of preventing increasingly sophisticated AI-driven cheating. President Lee Jae Myung's call on Friday for a swift overhaul of the national testing system accelerated efforts to move beyond multiple-choice exams and introduce written response and essay-based questions to Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam. In August, the National Education Commission presented Lee with a plan to consider introducing absolute grading and written response and essay-based questions to the CSAT. results.title: 1 election official arrested in alleged vote count manipulation case
results.content: A Seoul court on Tuesday issued an arrest warrant for a regional election official accused of concealing and forging a vote count sheet during the June 3 local elections. The Seoul Central District Court issued the warrant for the official, surnamed Lee, citing concerns that the suspect could destroy evidence. Lee was among eight officials -- three from the National Election Commission and five from regional election commissions -- accused of manipulating voter turnout figures or tampering with vote count records during the June 3 local elections. The court rejected warrant requests for the seven other officials, saying it was difficult to justify their detention. results.title: PM Han discusses ways to strengthen energy cooperation with Qatari minister
results.content: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook held a meeting with Qatari Minister of State for Energy Affairs Saad bin Sherida Al Kaabi on Monday to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation in renewable energy. During the meeting in Seoul, the South Korean prime minister recalled the development of mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries in the energy sector and expressed appreciation for Qatar's swift cooperation with South Korea in the energy sector following the outbreak of the Middle East conflict, her office said. Han also expressed expectations for expanded cooperation with Qatar in the renewable energy sector, including solar energy, while expressing hope that Qatar's emir, Tamim bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, would visit South Korea at an appropriate time. results.title: Seoul to offer up to 500 million won for reporting college entrance exam cheating
results.content: South Korea will offer rewards of up to 500 million won ($370,888) for reporting cheating on the annual college entrance exam, the anti-corruption agency said Monday, as authorities step up efforts to crack down on cheating aided by artificial intelligence (AI). The government will offer 100 million won for each tip-off that leads to the detection of a cheating case, up to a maximum of 500 million won, according to the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC). Those who confess to cheating and report accomplices will also receive the full reward, while facing reduced penalties for their own misconduct, the commission said. "The measure is aimed at safeguarding the fairness and credibility of the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by encouraging the public to report cheating," it said. results.title: SK hynix's US-traded shares surge after Nvidia CEO's reinstatement
results.content: WASHINGTON — U.S.-traded shares of South Korean chipmaker SK hynix Inc. surged 20 percent Monday following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer (CEO) of U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia Corp. SK hynix's American depositary receipts (ADRs), traded on the Nasdaq, jumped 20 percent, or $20.71, to finish at $124.28, according to market data. The sharp increase came after Nvidia announced Huang's reinstatement as CEO, a development that appeared to bolster investor confidence in the AI chipmaker and fuel buying interest in semiconductor-related stocks. results.title: Roasted tangerines? Korean actress shares surprising winter snack recipe
results.content: Click here for more articles by Kormedi.com. Actress So Yu-jin has recommended roasted tangerines as a winter snack. Recently, So shared a video on her social media showing how to prepare the treat, along with the caption, “Roasted tangerines. You must try these this winter. It brings out the sweetness!” The recipe transforms tangerines, traditionally peeled and eaten cold, into a warm seasonal delicacy. The preparation is simple. After washing the tangerines, she wrapped them in parchment paper and placed them in an air fryer. “Air fryer mode, 170 degrees Celsius for 20 minutes. No need to flip them,” she explained. When she cut open the finished tangerines, their moist flesh was visible inside the peel. results.title: AI-generated song's chart success draws mixed reactions
results.content: There may be no real person behind the voice singing the song, but the music itself remains. A song created using artificial intelligence (AI) has reached the top of Korea's largest music streaming platform. As AI-generated music wins over listeners and climbs to No. 1 on the charts, it is once again drawing attention to broader debates about the future of the music industry. “The Adult I Dreamed Of” by MEOMURU reached No. 1 on Melon's Top 100 chart on the afternoon of Nov. 13. It was the first AI-generated track to top the chart and maintained its position for more than a week, as of the afternoon of Nov. 20.
